findings.claim: User-contributed content is not distinguished from editorial because there is no editorial layer: the site supplies breadcrumb, field names and reader, the author supplies everything with meaning. phase2.argument: biohackrxiv is an A2 community site and holds no surface in the Phase 2 table, which draws its assignments from the original ten. Nothing seen argues for giving it one. Its single transferable idea, the named-field inventory that signals evidence quality by which slots are filled rather than by a badge (F29), belongs to the structured data blocks surface, which Stripe already governs with a stronger measured version: 61 collapsible field blocks with a per-block copy button against OSF's copyControls count of 0 (F39). Adding OSF as a secondary influence there would import a fixed empty-field skeleton (F37) that the uniqueness constraint forbids. It does sharpen one open item without filling it: the dossier contents rail and previews surface is unassigned under the stopping rule with Stripe proposed for the rail alone, and biohackrxiv is the negative case - a persistent left rail on a record page that carries application sections rather than the record's own thirteen headings, so the reader gets a permanent column that never points at what they are reading (F19, A5). That strengthens the existing stopping rule by confirming that a rail generated from the document's own headings is the requirement rather than one option among several. It supplies no observed hover-preview reference, so that part of the rule stands unchanged.

borrow.what: Signal evidence quality by inventory rather than by badge: name the questions a sceptical reader asks (is there human data, was it preregistered, who declared a conflict, what licence, what identifier) and let the answer be whether the slot is filled. Adapt to our stricter rule - absent data renders nothing, so the inventory becomes one labelled disclosure stating which slots this compound has and which it does not, never thirteen empty headings.

Identity as a two-state, not a badge: a resolvable identity renders as a link, a bare string renders as plain text, with no ornament added. Borrow it with the legend OSF omits, since an unexplained colour difference is not a signal. The meaning of OSF's two states is not stated on the page and could not be verified from the captures, which is exactly why the legend is the borrowable part.

Put the revision in the address: the breadcrumb reads "Preprints / BioHackrXiv / 5psfj_v2", so a reader can tell which revision they are on without opening a history panel. Published programme revisions should be addressable and named the same way in the visible path. Borrow the failure too: at 375 the breadcrumb is replaced by a hamburger and the revision id appears nowhere on the record's first screen (V2), so the revision must survive the mobile layout.
Truncation controls that name what they reveal: "See more" on a long author list, "Read more" on a cut abstract. One step, in place, and the control says what is behind it.

avoid.what: Anything placed in front of the search bar. On the mobile index the black "Add A Preprint" button sits above the tagline and the policy links while the search field lands at the bottom edge overlapped by a fixed Help pill. This is the concrete instance of the failure the freeze exists to prevent.

A browse grid heavier than the thing it sits under: four 100%-black subject tiles are the highest-contrast objects on the index and pull the eye past the search field above them. Filter chrome must sit at or below the weight of the records it filters.

A record page where the reader's window never moves and every evidence field stays below the first fold. Three desktop scroll captures at 0, 0.5 and 0.9 returned one identical file and no quality field appears in any capture at either viewport; whether an inner pane holds the scroll is not observable from the images. The dossier must scroll as one document, and nothing a reader needs to judge the evidence may sit behind a separate scroll region.

Embedding the document instead of structuring it. At 1.34% visible text to delivered HTML the page is a shell wrapped around a 65-page file it cannot search, quote or link into; our corpus sits at 8.3% and must rise.

A rail that carries application sections instead of the record's own headings: 300px of dark navy, 21% of the desktop width. It is record-aware - it expands to Preprints > Discover > Preprint details > Overview - but "Overview" is the only section it can name, so the record's thirteen headings appear in no rail anywhere.

A fixed help beacon over content: at 1440 it covers the lower right of the metadata card beside "Affiliated Institutions"; on the mobile index it overlaps the search field's top-right corner; on the mobile record it covers part of the embedded viewer's toolbar.
Unlabelled icon-only actions on a record: the download and share glyphs are the second thing seen on the mobile record and nothing names them.

An embedded document viewer as a record's only substance at 375: the viewer toolbar is clipped by the card and the fixed Help pill covers what remains, so the reader can neither page nor zoom the one copy of the content. Dossier evidence must be page text at 375, not a document reader.

notLongevityRelevantNote: BiohackrXiv publishes software written at biohackathons. The captured record is a federated-learning prototype for biobank infrastructure - no intervention, dose, organism, outcome measure or trial. It is not a source of longevity evidence and is useful to this study only as an information-design reference for how a platform frames a record it did not write.
